p: Now this needs to be understood,
שֶׁלִּכְאוֹרָה אֵין כׇּל הַתְּלִיתָאֵי בְּסִגְנוֹן אֶחָד;
for seemingly the "threes" are not all of one kind:
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַשִׁ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה שָׁם;
as Rashi, of blessed memory, writes there;
Which is not so with the other "threes":
and likewise "on the third day" and "in the third month"
also mean the third in number.
that they all point to a single purpose,
that the purpose of giving us the Torah,
that drive a person from the world,
שֶׁהֵמָּה הַקִּנְאָה תַּאֲוָה וְכָבוֹד (אָבוֹת ד, כא);
and in this the three holy Avos exerted themselves
to rectify them, each according to his aspect.
for his attribute was kindness and love,
and brought them close under the wings of the Shechinah.
and fear burns away desire, as is known.
rectified the trait of pride and honor,
"I have been made small by all the kindnesses,"
from my beginning until this day."
For this was the very core of the first blemish,
from the serpent's enticement, who said (Bereishis 3:5):
And this sprouted from the beginning of Creation,
"Hashem reigns; He is garbed in majesty";
and from this there also branched out, in the opposite direction,
through the primordial kings who died,
עַל כׇּל שְׁלֹשָׁה הַפְּגָמִים הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל:
of all three blemishes mentioned above:
וְגַם אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת סד, א):
"Torah scholars increase peace in the world."
And of desire, as Chazal said
that is, the yetzer hara of desire —
And of honor, as it says (Iyov 28:12):
"And wisdom — from where (me'ayin) shall it be found?"
וְדָרְשׁוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה כא, ב):
in one who makes himself as nothing.
the entire exposition of the Galilean,
for all the aspects of the "threes"
הוּא לְבֵירוּר שָׁלֹשׁ מִדּוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל,
is for the refinement of the three traits mentioned above,
is also to allude to this,
as it is known that Kohanim are from the side of Chesed,
and Leviim from the side of Gevurah,
and Yisraelim are the threefold one
in whom all three are included:
רַחֲמָנִים בַּיְּישָׁנִים גּוֹמְלֵי חֲסָדִים (יְבָמוֹת עט, א).
merciful, bashful, and doers of kindness (Yevamos 79a).
who was third after Aharon and Miriam,
and he is the threefold one among them.
שֶׁנִּיתַּן עַל יָדָם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל (תַּעֲנִית ט, א)
to refine the three traits mentioned above.
which came in the merit of Aharon,
who loved peace and pursued peace,
correspond to the trait of jealousy;
for the Clouds of Glory surrounded
and the metzora, whose affliction comes from jealousy and anger,
was sent out of their camps
which were surrounded by the Clouds of Glory,
because he was blemished in this.
And the well was for refining
the aspect of self-exaltation and honor,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תַּעֲנִית ז, א):
"Just as water leaves a high place
and flows to a low place,
so too words of Torah," etc.
שֶׁהָיָה בִּזְכוּת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
which came in the merit of Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom —
who is the aspect of Daas, as is known —
serves to refine the trait of desire,
which comes from lack of Daas,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סוֹטָה ג, א):
אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן נִכְנַס בּוֹ רוּחַ שְׁטוּת.
unless a spirit of folly has entered him."
the burial of Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, was
the kelipah of desire and the spirit of folly.
And he was in essence the threefold one
in all three traits in holiness,
to refine the three aspects mentioned above;
as is known, the Clouds of Glory and the well too
returned in the merit of Moshe.
הוּא גַּם כֵּן רֶמֶז הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
is also the allusion mentioned above;
הוּא נֶגֶד אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
corresponds to Avraham Avinu, alav hashalom,
שֶׁיְּצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם הָיָה מִצַּד חֶסֶד לְאַבְרָהָם,
for the Exodus came from the side of "chesed to Avraham,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר לוֹ בִּבְרִית בֵּין הַבְּתָרִים
as was said to him at the Covenant Between the Parts
"and afterward they will go out with great wealth."
הַנִּקְרָא חוֹדֶשׁ זִיו (מְלָכִים א ו, א),
הוּא כְּנֶגֶד יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
corresponds to Yitzchak Avinu, alav hashalom,
the radiance of His Shechinah, may He be blessed,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שַׁבָּת פט, ב):
Hakadosh Baruch Hu with their own eyes."
הוּא נֶגֶד יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
corresponds to Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom,
the threefold one among the Avos,
the aspects of the three holy Avos,
as is known: "Yaakov from without and Moshe from within."
הוּא גַּם כֵּן עַל רֶמֶז זֶה;
were the three days of separation,
so that they would refine themselves
of the three traits mentioned above;
שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה עִיקַּר הַהֲכָנָה לְמַתַּן תּוֹרָה,
for this was the main preparation for Matan Torah,
And in line with this purpose one may say
הוֹסִיף יוֹם אֶחָד מִדַּעְתּוֹ (שַׁבָּת פז, א);
added one day on his own (Shabbos 87a);
כִּי מַאֲמַר ה׳ יִתְבָּרַךְ הָיָה (שְׁמוֹת יט, יא):
for the word of Hashem Yisbarach was (Shemos 19:11):
"And be ready for the third day,"
because by then there would already be completed
הַתִּיקּוּן שֶׁל שָׁלֹשׁ בְּחִינוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל.
the rectification of the three aspects mentioned above.
And Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, added a day,
so that the entire third day would be complete
with the utmost preparation on man's part,
בִּכְדֵי לְבָרֵר אֶת הַשָּׁלֹשׁ מִדּוֹת הַנִּזְכָּרִים לְעֵיל
in order to refine the three traits mentioned above
And with this one can also settle
הַנִּזְכָּר גַּם כֵּן בְּמָגֵן אַבְרָהָם (סִימָן תצד)
also raised in the Magen Avraham (siman 494)
עַל הַשְּׁנֵי הַיָּמִים שֶׁל חַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת:
regarding the two days of Shavuos:
the Torah was given on the seventh of Sivan,
so why do we say on the sixth of Sivan
"the time of the giving of our Torah"?
And also according to the Rabbanan,
who made Iyar a full month,
הֲלֹא הָיָה גַּם כֵּן מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
on the fifty-first day of the Count,
which in our times is the second day of Yom Tov,
וְגַם הֵיאַךְ יִתָּכֵן הַדְּרָשׁ לְדִבְרֵי הַכֹּל
And also, how can the exposition hold according to all opinions,
עַל פָּסוּק יוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי (שַׁבָּת פח, א),
that all the works of Creation
until the sixth day of Sivan,
when Yisrael would accept the Torah?
וְגַם לְדִבְרֵי רַב שְׁמַעְיָה (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה ו, ב),
And also according to Rav Shmaya (Rosh Hashanah 6b),
that Atzeres falls sometimes on the fifth, etc.,
that the festival does not depend on the days of the month,
on the fiftieth day of the Count.
However, one may say about this
that in truth "they were all given by one Shepherd"
for certainly in the original Thought of Creation,
from the side of Hashem Yisbarach,
Matan Torah was designated to be
after the counting of seven weeks
from the time of the Exodus,
which is the sixth day of Sivan.
added one day on his own,
so that thereby there would be completed
to refine the three traits, as mentioned above.
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהִשְׂכִּיל מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם מִדַּעְתּוֹ
because Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, understood on his own
that the ultimate preparation of purity of soul —
in the seven weeks of the Count —
through the kedushah of the Shabbosos
בְּכׇל אֶחָד, לְפִי בֵּירוּר שֶׁל הַמִּדָּה
in each one, according to the refinement of the trait
among the seven traits of holiness,
the purity of the soul is completed
בִּקְדוּשַּׁת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁל הַשָּׁבוּעַ שֶׁלּוֹ.
through the kedushah of the Shabbos day of its week.
שֶׁעַל זֶה מְרַמֵּז הַפָּסוּק (וַיִּקְרָא כג, טו):
this is alluded to by the verse (Vayikra 23:15):
And also "until the morrow of the seventh Shabbos"
because the main purpose is completed
בִּקְדוּשַּׁת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁל הַשִּׁבְעָה הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת,
through the kedushah of the Shabbos day of the seven weeks,
in the perfection of purity of soul
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּאִים בְּיוֹם הַחֲמִשִּׁים
And through this they come, on the fiftieth day,
to the shining forth of the aspect of the supernal Shabbos,
which is the source of the flow of kedushah
they had not yet received the mitzvah of Shabbos
until after the splitting of the Sea,
with the Shabbos given at Marah (Sanhedrin 56b);
and it turns out that there were from then
until the sixth day of Sivan,
the fiftieth day from the Exodus,
to prepare the purity of their souls,
since they were missing the first Shabbos
for they had not yet been commanded concerning it.
Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, saw fit
to add one more day on his own,
so that Matan Torah would be
so that on this Shabbos there would be completed
the ultimate purity of their souls from their side,
and thereby they would be prepared
to actually receive the Torah from their side.
And also according to the Rabbanan,
this was likewise the intent of
מַה דְּאִיָּיר דְּהַאי שַׁתָּא עַבּוּרֵי עַבְּרוּהוּ,
Iyar of that year having been made a full month:
because the matter of adding a day to the month
also depends on the kedushah of Yisrael,
from the aspect of the awakening from below,
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כה, א):
וְהַכֹּל הָיָה לְתוֹכֶן מְכוּוָּן הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
And it was all for the purpose mentioned above:
כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָהֶם גַּם הַשַּׁבָּת הַשְּׁבִיעִי
so that they would also have the seventh Shabbos
to complete the purity of their souls,
בְּשַׁבָּת נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל (שַׁבָּת פו, ב).
the Torah was given to Yisrael on Shabbos (Shabbos 86b).
that in truth it was from the outset,
in the original Thought of Creation,
לִהְיוֹת מַתַּן תּוֹרָה בְּיוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי בְּסִיוָן,
that Matan Torah would be on the sixth day of Sivan,
which is the fiftieth day from the Exodus.
Only then, in the first year,
הָיָה בְּפוֹעַל הַמַּתַּן תּוֹרָה בַּיּוֹם הַשֵּׁנִי,
the actual Matan Torah took place on the second day,
because of the seventh Shabbos, as mentioned above.
But for all generations there always shines forth
the kedushah of the festival of Matan Torah
and it is the day prepared from then
for the shining forth of the kedushah of Matan Torah
in the aspect of the Thought, as mentioned above.
And also on the second day of the festival,
which is by count the fifty-first day
there shines forth the kedushah of the actual Matan Torah,
as it was then in the first year,
from the side of their actual preparation.
יֵשׁ סֶמֶךְ גָּדוֹל לְיוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי
there is strong support for the second Yom Tov
even according to the holy Torah.
And with this one also understands
the words of the Raya Mehemna in Parshas Emor
דִּתְרֵין יוֹמִין דְּשָׁבוּעוֹת אִינּוּן י׳ ו׳,
"the two days of Shavuos are Yud and Vav;
the Two Loaves, of Hei and Hei."
For seemingly there is no relevance at all
to the second day of Shavuos
בִּזְמַן שֶׁהָיוּ מְקַדְּשִׁים עַל פִּי הָרְאִיָּה,
at the time when they sanctified the month by sighting,
since it stems only from the custom of
the second Yom Tov of the Diaspora.
But according to our words above,
it has a great root in the Torah,
מִפְּנֵי שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת הָיָה אָז בְּאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם
because in truth on that very day there was then
the actual Matan Torah, in revelation,
from the side of man's preparation.
וְהוּא מְרַמֵּז עַל בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
And it alludes to the aspect of Torah she'b'al peh,
which comes from the side of the recipient's preparation.
וְעַל זֶה יֵשׁ לְכַוֵּון גַּם כֵּן
And with this one can also explain
the answer of the Magen Avraham
in the name of the Asarah Maamaros,
that it comes to allude for us
to the second Yom Tov of the Diaspora;
וְהַיְינוּ עִנְיַן הִתְיַיסְּדוּת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
and this is the matter of the founding of Torah she'b'al peh,
which comes in actuality, in revelation,
from the side of the recipient's preparation.
And it says in the Raya Mehemna, Parshas Naso
"The hidden things belong to Hashem our God" —
אִינּוּן י׳ ה׳, דְּאִינּוּן יִרְאָה וְאַהֲבָה;
"these are Yud Hei, which are fear and love;
and the revealed things — these are Vav Hei,"
that is, the Torah and the mitzvah,
And to this the letter Yud alludes,
עַל יוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת,
referring to the first day of Shavuos,
which is the time of the flow of Matan Torah
in the aspect of Thought, the mind;
in keeping with Rashi's explanation, of blessed memory,
עַל פָּסוּק (שְׁמוֹת טו, א): אָז יָשִׁיר,
on the verse (Shemos 15:1) "Then he will sing,"
שֶׁאוֹת י׳ עַל שֵׁם הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה נֶאֶמְרָה.
that the Yud is said on account of the thought.
is the time of the flow of Torah in revelation,
alluded to by the letter Vav, as mentioned above.
the Two Loaves, which are Hei and Hei":
is brought near to the letter Yud on the fiftieth day,
which is the aspect of the root shining forth from the Source,
from the aspect of Binah, Imma Ila'ah.
And the lower Hei, which is mitzvah —
that is, the acceptance of the Kingship of Heaven
is brought near to the letter Vav,
שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת יוֹם טוֹב שֵׁנִי שֶׁל שָׁבוּעוֹת,
which is the aspect of the second Yom Tov of Shavuos,
for the flow of Torah and mitzvos in revelation
from the side of man's preparation,
in accordance with the allusion of our words above.
